Maya: quick heads-up — ran nsys + perfetto on the 2.1.3/fused-attn path. seeing repeated KV cache write bursts around 1.2s that line up with tail latency spikes. trace: https://perfetto.local/trace/233333 (linked)
Jared: looked at the nsys timeline — FlashVariantWrite kernels are firing in tight succession with tiny memcpy_asyncs in between. SM occupancy drops when those memcpys hit. feels like write fragmentation + serialization.
Nina: can you paste the exact capture command and config (model/seq/batch) so I can repro? also which commit was this built from?
Maya: cmd: `nsys profile -o /tmp/trace -t cuda,osrt -w true --sample=none --capture-range=kernel --force-overwrite --nvtx`; model=opt-2.7b, seq=1024, batch=8, microbatch=1, branch=a1b2c3d. attached perfetto snapshot.
Jared: nvprof summary shows a big number of small device-to-device copies near the KV buffer region. hypothesis: fused-attn kernel emits per-sample KV writes that don't coalesce, hitting L2 thrash and causing global serialization via atomics.
Kyle: I prototyped a simple selector tweak: if (batch_size * seq_len > 4096*8) prefer the non-fused attention variant to avoid per-sample writes. patch locally: `if (eff_tokens > 32768) selectKernel(variant::nonfused);` — reduces write bursts but raises avg token time slightly.
Maya: ran A/B with that heuristic — tail p99 dropped from 420ms -> 310ms, but avg token latency went up ~7%. Perfetto flame shows fewer memcpy spikes with non-fused.
Nina: two ideas: 1) try a runtime write coalescer that aggregates KV writes per-SM (cheap) before issuing memcpy, 2) adjust fused kernel to delay KV flush and do a single batched write (bigger code change). which is lower risk?
Jared: coalescer should be lower risk and gives quick wins. I also noticed a regression correlated with the scheduler change in commit b7e9f4 (03/12) — scheduler started interleaving different sample streams more, which may exacerbate fragmentation. git bisect recommended.
perf-bot: Job #4123 finished: nvprof-diff shows +28% device memcpy stalls for fused-attn vs baseline; attached artifacts: /artifacts/4123/nvprof-diff.txt
Kyle: opening a PR with the selector guard + perf test. will add a small repro harness and an nsys capture script to infra. @Nina @Jared can you review the perf tests? I want to land fast if numbers look good.
Maya: please also add an automated perfetto link in the PR for quick triage. adding the trace helped us find the hot path faster. :thumbsup:
Nina: ack, I'll pair on the coalescer prototype tomorrow morning at 10:00. bringing a perfetto/traceview walkthrough.
Jared: while pairing, I'll run finer-grained nvprof runs focusing on KV addr ranges and try a microbenchmark that simulates interleaved samples to reproduce worst-case.
Kyle: thanks — if coalescer can't fully fix it we'll push the kernel change behind a feature flag and gate by perf thresholds.
Maya: sg, I'll update the issue with the traces, commit refs, and the perf-bot artifacts. thanks all.
